tool_summary: Creates a new user account on the system.
platform_notes: useradd is a GNU/Linux (shadow-utils) tool; macOS has no direct equivalent (dscl is used instead). This ruleset targets Linux only.

rules.description: The -o/--non-unique flag combined with a -u/--uid value of 0 creates a second account sharing root's UID, granting it full root privileges without going through the root account itself.
rules.notes: This is a well-known privilege escalation / backdoor pattern: a second root-equivalent account that is easy to overlook in audits.

rules.description: Creates a new user account. This expands the system's attack surface and, depending on group membership and shell assigned, may grant meaningful system access.
rules.reversible_note: The account can be removed with userdel, but any access granted or actions taken under it before removal are not undone.
